root_cause.text: The Marvell MVEBU GPIO suspend/resume paths unconditionally called PWM helper functions on every GPIO bank, even though some banks have `mvchip->mvpwm == NULL`, leading to a NULL-pointer dereference in `mvebu_pwm_suspend()`/`mvebu_pwm_resume()` when accessing PWM state.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `if (IS_REACHABLE(CONFIG_PWM))` to `if (IS_REACHABLE(CONFIG_PWM) && mvchip->mvpwm)` in both `mvebu_gpio_suspend()` and `mvebu_gpio_resume()`, and the CVE text states that “GPIO banks without PWM have mvchip->mvpwm set to NULL” and calling suspend with `mvpwm == NULL` dereferences `mvpwm->blink_select`.

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: The Marvell MVEBU GPIO suspend/resume paths unconditionally called PWM helper functions on every GPIO bank, even though some banks have `mvchip->mvpwm == NULL`, leading to a NULL-pointer dereference in `mvebu_pwm_suspend()`/`mvebu_pwm_resume()` when accessing PWM state.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch changes `if (IS_REACHABLE(CONFIG_PWM))` to `if (IS_REACHABLE(CONFIG_PWM) && mvchip->mvpwm)` in both `mvebu_gpio_suspend()` and `mvebu_gpio_resume()`, and the CVE text states that “GPIO banks without PWM have mvchip->mvpwm set to NULL” and calling suspend with `mvpwm == NULL` dereferences `mvpwm->blink_select`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a null/ არსებence check before suspending PWM support in the mvebu GPIO suspend path.
intent_record.what: In `mvebu_gpio_suspend()`, the call to `mvebu_pwm_suspend(mvchip)` was changed from being conditional only on `IS_REACHABLE(CONFIG_PWM)` to requiring both `IS_REACHABLE(CONFIG_PWM)` and `mvchip->mvpwm` to be true.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the suspend path will now skip PWM suspend handling unless the device actually has an associated PWM instance. This prevents dereferencing or operating on a missing PWM pointer during suspend.

intent_record.intent_summary: Guard the PWM resume path so it only runs when the PWM instance exists.
intent_record.what: In `mvebu_gpio_resume(struct platform_device *pdev)`, the conditional call to `mvebu_pwm_resume(mvchip)` was changed from `if (IS_REACHABLE(CONFIG_PWM))` to `if (IS_REACHABLE(CONFIG_PWM) && mvchip->mvpwm)`, adding a check that `mvchip->mvpwm` is non-NULL before invoking the PWM resume helper.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the resume path now skips PWM resume unless the PWM object is actually present, preventing a null-pointer dereference or invalid resume call on devices/chips without an associated PWM instance.

grouping_result.intent: Add a null/ არსებence check before suspending PWM support in the mvebu GPIO suspend path.
Guard the PWM resume path so it only runs when the PWM instance exists.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it adds a NULL/ არსებence check before calling PWM suspend logic in the MVEBU GPIO suspend path, preventing the NULL-pointer dereference when a bank has no PWM instance.
The change directly matches the root cause by adding a guard around the PWM resume path to avoid calling PWM helpers when mvchip->mvpwm is NULL, which prevents the NULL-pointer dereference.

candidates.rationale: This unconditionally invokes the PWM suspend helper in the GPIO suspend path. For GPIO banks where mvchip->mvpwm is NULL, the helper later dereferences a NULL PWM pointer, causing the crash described in the root cause.
This unconditionally invokes the PWM resume helper in the GPIO resume path. When mvchip->mvpwm is NULL for some banks, this leads to a NULL-pointer dereference inside the PWM resume logic.

vuln_statements.explanation: This unconditionally calls the PWM suspend helper for every GPIO bank. For banks where mvchip->mvpwm is NULL, the helper dereferences a null PWM pointer, matching the reported suspend-path crash.
This unconditionally calls the PWM resume helper for every GPIO bank. For banks where mvchip->mvpwm is NULL, the helper dereferences a null PWM pointer, matching the reported resume-path crash.

bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 757642f9a584e893f3f4e50c99b674ee8a3ed363
Author: Andrew Lunn <andrew@lunn.ch>
Date:   Fri Apr 14 17:40:52 2017 +0200

    gpio: mvebu: Add limited PWM support
    
    Armada 370/XP devices can 'blink' GPIO lines with a configurable on
    and off period. This can be modelled as a PWM.
    
    However, there are only two sets of PWM configuration registers for
    all the GPIO lines. This driver simply allows a single GPIO line per
    GPIO chip of 32 lines to be used as a PWM. Attempts
bic_trace_step.reason: The shown suspend/resume code already guards the PWM paths by calling them only when PWM is enabled and after PWM probe has potentially populated mvchip->mvpwm. The relevant lines are: `if (IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_PWM)) mvebu_pwm_suspend(mvchip);` and `if (IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_PWM)) mvebu_pwm_resume(mvchip);`. In this commit, the PWM helper functions themselves dereference `mvchip->mvpwm` (`struct mvebu_pwm *mvpwm = mvchip->mvpwm;`), but the diff does not show the vulnerable unconditional suspend/resume call on every GPIO bank without checking for NULL. Since the root cause describes a NULL-pointer dereference caused by unconditionally calling PWM helpers on banks where `mvchip->mvpwm == NULL`, and that exact unsafe construct is not present here, the vulnerable construct is absent. The code also reflects the intended fix path by gating the suspend/resume calls on CONFIG_PWM and wiring PWM support only via `mvebu_pwm_probe()` for compatible hardware.

commit 757642f9a584e893f3f4e50c99b674ee8a3ed363
Author: Andrew Lunn <andrew@lunn.ch>

    gpio: mvebu: Add limited PWM support
    
    Armada 370/XP devices can 'blink' GPIO lines with a configurable on
    and off period. This can be modelled as a PWM.
    
    However, there are only two sets of PWM configuration registers for
    all the GPIO lines. This driver simply allows a single GPIO line per
    GPIO chip of 32 lines to be used as a PWM. Attempts
bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet clearly shows the vulnerable suspend/resume behavior: in both paths the driver unconditionally calls the PWM helpers whenever CONFIG_PWM is enabled, with no NULL check on mvchip->mvpwm: `if (IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_PWM)) mvebu_pwm_suspend(mvchip);` and `if (IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_PWM)) mvebu_pwm_resume(mvchip);`. The helper functions themselves immediately dereference `mvchip->mvpwm` (`struct mvebu_pwm *mvpwm = mvchip->mvpwm;`) and access it (`mvpwm->blink_select = ...`, `mvpwm->blink_on_duration = ...`, etc.), so if a GPIO bank has `mvchip->mvpwm == NULL` this would fault. The fix is not present here because there is no guard such as `if (mvchip->mvpwm)` or per-bank handling before calling the PWM suspend/resume helpers.
